name: paper-my-code
description: Light and dark paper themes in print colours, with an optional realistic paper texture, ink spread and light scattering over the editor.

commands.title: Toggle Ink Spread and Light Scattering

enumDescriptions: Smooth drawing paper: fine grain, some fibres.
Cold-press watercolour paper: pronounced rounded tooth.
Japanese kozo paper: long visible fibres in a thin, cloudy sheet.
Laid writing paper: wire marks about 10 per cm, chain lines every 20-30 mm.
Grey board: pressed recycled fibre, lumps and uneven pressing.
Coarse artist canvas: plain weave, about 11 threads per cm.
paperMyCode.paper.markdownDescription: The paper, for the texture and ink spread. Each one is generated once (a few seconds) and cached. Takes effect with **Paper my Code: Turn On Paper**.

paperMyCode.texture.enabled.markdownDescription: **Paper texture**: a shaded relief of tooth, fibres and pulp formation, lit from the upper left. Shadows show on light surfaces, highlights on dark ones.

paperMyCode.texture.intensity.markdownDescription: Strength of the relief. Subtle on purpose: it changes light areas by only a few levels. Screens with low contrast may need more.

paperMyCode.texture.darkBalance.markdownDescription: How strong the relief is on dark surfaces, relative to light ones.

paperMyCode.texture.grain.markdownDescription: Pixel-fine fibres and grain on top, which keep the rounded tooth from looking like leather.

paperMyCode.mottle.enabled.markdownDescription: **Ink mottle**: lightens dark areas in soft patches, where ink soaked in unevenly.

paperMyCode.printColors.enabled.markdownDescription: **Print colours**: limits the themes' colours to what offset print on uncoated paper can reach. Blues, violets and bright greens get much calmer, reds and yellows stay strong, greys don't change.

paperMyCode.printColors.strength.markdownDescription: How far colours move into the print gamut.

paperMyCode.matte.enabled.markdownDescription: **Matte**: the blacks of print instead of a screen. Even the darkest ink reflects some light, so the themes' shadows lift and turn to charcoal at the maximum, while midtones and white stay. White gets a touch warmer.

paperMyCode.matte.strength.markdownDescription: Strength of the matte look; `1` is the black of uncoated paper.

paperMyCode.inkSpread.enabled.markdownDescription: **Ink spread**: dark strokes in the editor grow a little where the paper takes ink, with ragged edges, like ink on absorbent paper. Takes effect with **Turn On Paper**.

paperMyCode.lightScatter.enabled.markdownDescription: **Light scattering**: light entering the paper next to ink scatters under it, so dark strokes in the editor get a faint soft halo and light gaps between them get a little darker. Sized from the scattering length of uncoated paper.

enumDescriptions: The whole window: editors, sidebars, panels, terminal, menus.
Only the editor area. Webviews (Markdown preview and the like) stay uncovered.
paperMyCode.scope.markdownDescription: Where the paper texture goes. Ink spread and light scattering are always on the editor's text only.

enumDescriptions: For HiDPI displays (150 % and up): twice the relief detail, grain one device pixel fine.

paperMyCode.scale.markdownDescription: **True size**: the textures are made for a pixel of 0.23 mm (110 dpi at 100 % scaling). For true size set this to your screen's dpi ÷ (110 × display scaling), e.g. `1.27` for a 27" 4K screen at 150 %. Keep laid paper and canvas at whole numbers, as regular patterns shimmer otherwise.

paperMyCode.hideInFullscreen.markdownDescription: Hide the texture while VSCodium is fullscreen (presenting, screen sharing).

paperMyCode.shiftTexture.markdownDescription: Start the texture at a random position every time it's applied, so on OLED screens its light and dark spots don't wear in one place.
